display_title: Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

head_commit.message:
Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

This update enables building and testing JAX with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support, and introduces Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels.

ROCm and oneAPI still rely on dynamically linked libstdc++ and C++17 to compile properly.

Other fixes and changes
### 1. Fix `-Wmissing-constinit` in C++20
File: `xla/tsl/profiler/convert/oss/xla_op_utils.cc`
- **Error:** xla/tsl/profiler/convert/oss/xla_op_utils.cc:24:29: error: 'constinit' specifier missing on initializing declaration of 'kHloSparseCoreV0Infeed' [-Werror,-Wmissing-constinit]
- **Cause & Fix:** In C++20 mode, `ABSL_CONST_INIT` expands to `constinit`. When a variable is declared `ABSL_CONST_INIT extern const` in `xla_op_utils.h`, C++20 requires `constinit` on the initializing definition as well. Added `TF_CONST_INIT` to the definitions in `xla_op_utils.cc`.

### 2. Fix `-Wthread-safety-analysis` with `libc++` in cuDNN Frontend
File: `third_party/cudnn_frontend_header_fix.patch`
- **Error:** include/cudnn_frontend_Heuristics.h:277:16: error: mutex 'EngineHeuristics_v8::get_heur_b_mutex()' is not held on every path through here [-Werror,-Wthread-safety-analysis] include/cudnn_frontend_Heuristics.h:280:49: error: releasing mutex 'EngineHeuristics_v8::get_heur_b_mutex()' that was not held [-Werror,-Wthread-safety-analysis]
- **Cause & Fix:** Unlike `libstdc++`, `libc++` annotates `std::mutex` with Clang thread-safety attributes (`capability("mutex")`). In `EngineHeuristicsBuilder_v8::build()`, `cudnn-frontend` conditionally locked and unlocked `get_heur_b_mutex()` in two separate `if (m_heuristics.mode == CUDNN_HEUR_MODE_B)` blocks around `detail::finalize(...)`. Replaced the split `.lock()` / `.unlock()` calls with a scoped `std::lock_guard<std::mutex>`.

### 3. Fix oneDNN (`mkl_dnn`) `Log1p` Numerical Mismatch with `libc++`
Files: `third_party/mkl_dnn/eltwise_injector_lower_bound.patch`, `third_party/mkl_dnn/workspace.bzl`
- **Error:** FAIL: //xla/tests:exhaustive_op_test_f32_cpu (Log1p numerical mismatch)
- **Cause & Fix:** oneDNN's JIT eltwise injector (`jit_uni_eltwise_injector` on `x64` and `aarch64`) stores multiple constant table entries under the same key in a `std::multimap` (`entry_map_`) and accesses subsequent entries by adding `key_off_val_shift` to the first entry's offset. It used `entry_map_.find(key)`, which is not guaranteed by the C++ standard to return the first matching element in a `std::multimap` (and under `libc++` returned an interior RB-tree node, reading the wrong polynomial coefficients). Replaced `entry_map_.find(key)` with `entry_map_.lower_bound(key)` to guarantee returning the first element for `key`.

### 4. Fix `nvJitLink` Register Spill Detection on CUDA 13.4.1
File: `xla/stream_executor/cuda/nvjitlink.cc`
- **Error:** FAILED: //xla/stream_executor/cuda:compilation_provider_test_without_gpu CompilationProviderTest.CancelIfRegSpill/nvjitlink
- **Cause & Fix:** In CUDA 13.4.1, `nvJitLinkComplete()` can return `NVJITLINK_SUCCESS` even when the error log contains `ptxas` register spill diagnostics. Updated `nvjitlink.cc` to always fetch `nvJitLinkGetErrorLog(link_handle)` and check it via `CreateErrorFromPTXASLog(...)` regardless ofwhether `linking_result` is `NVJITLINK_SUCCESS`.

display_title: When `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleReduceWindow` folds a `kPad` into a `kReduceWindow`, `is_effective_broadcast` replaces the pair with a broadcast of the unpadded operand. The check previously inspected only the `kPad` configuration and ignored existing padding and window dilation on the `kReduceWindow` itself. When the `kReduceWindow` also carried window padding, output windows that covered only padding elements were rewritten to the operand value. Window padding on dimensions larger than 1 also triggered a crash in `CreateBroadcastSequence`.

head_commit.message:
When `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleReduceWindow` folds a `kPad` into a `kReduceWindow`, `is_effective_broadcast` replaces the pair with a broadcast of the unpadded operand. The check previously inspected only the `kPad` configuration and ignored existing padding and window dilation on the `kReduceWindow` itself. When the `kReduceWindow` also carried window padding, output windows that covered only padding elements were rewritten to the operand value. Window padding on dimensions larger than 1 also triggered a crash in `CreateBroadcastSequence`.

Compute the combined `Window` first and check `is_effective_broadcast` against that combined window and static shapes. Require trivial windows on dimensions not equal to 1, reject window dilation or negative padding on size 1 dimensions, and check endpoint window coverage. Existing programs whose combined window covers a single unpadded element surrounded by identity padding still fold to broadcast.

construction.

are preserved, and add a parameterized unit test in `gemv_rewriter_test.cc`
covering a vector-matrix dot with a `> 2^31` dimension.

head_commit.message:
Preserve 64-bit constant indices in ShouldFuseInPlaceOp

In InstructionFusion::ShouldFuseInPlaceOp, get_constant_operand narrowed
LiteralBase::GetFirstInteger() from std::optional<int64_t> to
std::optional<int>. For tensors with >2^31 elements, 64-bit constant
offsets congruent modulo 2^32 (such as 1 and 2^32 + 1) falsely matched
when fusing slice or dynamic-slice into dynamic-update-slice, while
matching 64-bit slice and dynamic-update-slice offsets >2^31 failed to
fuse.

Change get_constant_operand to return std::optional<int64_t> in
xla/service/instruction_fusion.cc and add unit tests in
xla/service/instruction_fusion_test.cc covering >32-bit constant
offsets.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use 64-bit dimensions in CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm.

`CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm` in `xla/service/cpu/dot_op_emitter.cc` narrowed the
GEMM dimensions `m`, `k`, and `n` from `int64_t` to 32-bit `int` before

dimensions `>= 2^31` that wrap negative in 32-bit `int` or dimensions `> 2^32`

`SmallWhileLoopHoistingPass` to treat them as inlineable small GEMMs.

Widen `m`, `k`, and `n` to `int64_t` in `CanEmitTiledLlvmIrGemm`, and add
symbolic HLO unit tests in
`xla/service/cpu/small_while_loop_hoisting_pass_test.cc`.

When `WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion` sinks an `all-reduce` feeding a
`dynamic-update-slice` out of a `while` loop, `UpdateSliceContext`

to `int64_t` so 64-bit slice offsets are preserved without narrowing.

name: CI
display_title: Fix stack buffer overflow in IsFabricMemory

head_commit.message:
Fix stack buffer overflow in IsFabricMemory

`IsFabricMemory` reads `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES` into a 4-byte `unsigned int`, but the driver writes a 64-bit value. So the call overwrites the 4 bytes after `handle_types` on the stack. In an x86-64 build with `-Os`, these are the low 4 bytes of the caller's saved `rbx` register.

This only leads to a crash if the caller keeps a live value in `rbx` across the call. After an unrelated change shifted register allocation, `CudaStream::Memcpy` now keeps its `ActivateContext` pointer in `rbx` and segfaults when it destroys that pointer.

So this change makes `handle_types` a `uint64_t`. The CUDA documentation doesn't state the type of this attribute, but NCCL and UCX both read it into a 64-bit integer.

I also added tests to `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver_test.cc` that only use driver API calls. For every pointer attribute and memory pool attribute that stream executor queries, they measure how many bytes the driver writes and compare that to the size of the variable that stream executor uses. They cover device, pinned host, pageable host, managed and VMM memory, and both `cuPointerGetAttribute` and `cuPointerGetAttributes`. Apart from `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES`, all of these variables already had the right size.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Only fuse AMAX reductions into cuDNN convolution fusions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Only fuse AMAX reductions into cuDNN convolution fusions

With --xla_gpu_experimental_enable_conv_fusion, ConvFusionRewriter fused any
scalar reduce that follows a convolution, and CuDnnFusionCompiler emitted
every fused reduce as a cuDNN AMAX reduction without looking at the reducer
or the init value. sum, max and min of a convolution therefore returned the
maximum absolute value of the convolution output.

Add IsCudnnAmaxReduce, which only accepts the pattern the compiler
implements (f32 maximum over abs(x) with a zero or -inf init), use it to decide
whether a reduce can be an epilogue, and make the compiler return
Unimplemented for any other reduce instead of building an AMAX node.

Fixes #50470.

`IsFabricMemory` reads `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES` into a 4-byte `unsigned int`, but the driver writes a 64-bit value. So the call overwrites the 4 bytes after `handle_types` on the stack. In an x86-64 build with `-Os`, these are the low 4 bytes of the caller's saved `rbx` register.

This only leads to a crash if the caller keeps a live value in `rbx` across the call. After an unrelated change shifted register allocation, `CudaStream::Memcpy` now keeps its `ActivateContext` pointer in `rbx` and segfaults when it destroys that pointer.

So this change makes `handle_types` a `uint64_t`. The CUDA documentation doesn't state the type of this attribute, but NCCL and UCX both read it into a 64-bit integer.

I also added tests to `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver_test.cc` that only use driver API calls. For every pointer attribute and memory pool attribute that stream executor queries, they measure how many bytes the driver writes and compare that to the size of the variable that stream executor uses. They cover device, pinned host, pageable host, managed and VMM memory, and both `cuPointerGetAttribute` and `cuPointerGetAttributes`. Apart from `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES`, all of these variables already had the right size.

[XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

`EstimateNumWarps` picks the warp count from the largest padded tile in the fusion. Broadcasts, `iota` and narrow intermediates such as `pred` comparisons feeding a reduction inflate that size by 4x or more, which selects 4-8 warps where 2-4 are faster.

display_title: Avoid recursion in EmitInstruction for indexing and elementwise ops

head_commit.message:
Avoid recursion in EmitInstruction for indexing and elementwise ops

`SubgraphConverter::EmitInstruction` only used an iterative worklist for elementwise ops. Indexing ops like `bitcast`, `transpose`, `reshape` and `slice` still recursed through `HloToMlir` and the operand provider, which costs a few KiB of stack per op. So a long enough chain of these ops inside a single fusion overflows the stack of the compiling thread. (We've seen fusions with chains of a few hundred bitcasts when `algsimp` is disabled.)

Therefore this change computes the operand indices when an instruction gets pushed onto the work stack and emits all in-subgraph operands iteratively before lowering the instruction itself. Ops with dedicated emitters (`pad`, `concatenate`, `dynamic-slice`, `reduce`, etc.) still request their operands through the operand provider, so chains of those still recurse. `HasDedicatedEmitter` is now the single list of these ops, and `HloToMlir` checks that it got indices for every operand otherwise.

The emission order changes from a reverse BFS to a DFS post-order. After canonicalization and CSE the IR is the same for all existing tests.

This also fixes two latent issues of the old elementwise worklist:

1. It emitted the broadcasted scalar operands of `select` and `clamp` with the full-rank output indices, which produced invalid IR like `tensor.extract %arg0[%x, %y] : tensor<i8>`. This went unnoticed because canonicalization removed the dead op before anything verified it.
2. Operands could get emitted twice because the reverse loop called `HloToMlir` without checking the cache first.

To catch issues like the first one, the test now verifies the IR before canonicalization.

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Rematerialize from a saved copy when an operand's storage is overwritten

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Rematerialize from a saved copy when an operand's storage is overwritten

When rematerialization runs after copy insertion, a while body's parameter
element may share storage with the matching root element. Rematerialization
did not know this. It could recompute a reader of the parameter after the
root element's producer had overwritten it, so the recomputation read the
next iteration's value and silently produced wrong results.

The new `Options::alias_info` makes rematerialization run HloAliasAnalysis
and record which instruction overwrites each operand's storage. A
recomputation is placed before an overwriter that has not run yet, with a
control edge. If the overwriter already ran, a single view array operand is saved to
a copy right before the overwrite and the recomputation reads the copy; tuple
and multi view operands are not recomputed past the overwrite. The copy's
size is charged to the candidate, so recomputing must still pay off. Only
rejecting such candidates can leave a program over the memory limit.

Overwriters, the definers of overwritten values, and in place updates of
their own operand are not rematerialized. Without `alias_info` the pass
behaves as before.

display_title: [XLA:CI] Enable Bazel timestamps, progress rate limit, and remote gRPC logging in CI.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CI] Enable Bazel timestamps, progress rate limit, and remote gRPC logging in CI.

**Status quo**
`_DEFAULT_BAZEL_OPTIONS` in `third_party/xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` does not enable console timestamps (`--show_timestamps`), progress rate limiting (`--show_progress_rate_limit`), or remote gRPC call logging (`--experimental_remote_grpc_log`), and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not upload Bazel diagnostic logs when a CI job fails or is cancelled.

**Why**
When a test action hangs in RBE until the 60-minute GitHub Actions step timeout, the console log lacks wall-clock timestamps and RBE gRPC stream details (`ActionDigest`, operation name, and `ExecuteOperationMetadata.stage` transitions), and `profile.json.gz` is discarded when the container exits.

**Design choices**
- Add `show_timestamps=True`, `show_progress_rate_limit=5`, and `experimental_remote_grpc_log="bazel_remote_grpc.log"` to `_DEFAULT_BAZEL_OPTIONS` in `third_party/xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` and regenerate `third_party/xla/build_tools/ci/golden_commands.txt`.
- Add an `Upload Bazel diagnostic logs` step with `if: failure() || cancelled()` in `third_party/xla/.github/workflows/ci.yml` to upload `profile.json.gz` and `bazel_remote_grpc.log` as workflow artifacts per matrix job.

**Compromises**
- Writing `bazel_remote_grpc.log` adds a few megabytes of disk I/O during RBE builds, and artifacts are only uploaded when a job fails or is cancelled.

**Alternatives**
- Enabling `--subcommands` (`-s`): rejected because printing full command lines for thousands of compile and link actions floods the GitHub Actions console log without recording RBE gRPC stream state.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Compute the collapsed stride of symbolic reshape tiles

Note: flagged and fixed by AI.

In symbolic mode, a collapse always used the stride of the innermost dimension. A symbolic tile size is not the constant 1, so the old check did not skip untiled dimensions. A following expand then computed wrong tile sizes. Thus the register pre-check could reject valid tilings.

Changes:

*   Collapse, symbolic mode: select the stride with a symbolic `tile size > 1` indicator.
*   Collapse, concrete mode: simplify the source tiles with their constraints first. Before, some unit tile sizes did not simplify to 1, and the stride was wrong.
*   Reduce-scatter and all-to-all, symbolic mode: reject only a constant stride that is not 1.
*   Expand and reduce-scatter, symbolic mode: do not use `operator-` or `Canonicalize()`. They took exponential time on the new stride.

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.

display_title: Initialize results of pointer attribute queries in CudaExecutor

head_commit.message:
Initialize results of pointer attribute queries in CudaExecutor

`cuPointerGetAttributes` returns `CUDA_SUCCESS` for pageable host memory but doesn't write `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_RANGE_START_ADDR` and `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_RANGE_SIZE`, even though the documentation says that the attributes get assigned default NULL values in that case. `CudaExecutor::IsHostMemoryPinned` only reads the range if the memory type is `CU_MEMORYTYPE_HOST`, so today it never reads the uninitialized values. But that's only due to the order of the checks.

So this change initializes the results in `IsHostMemoryPinned` to 0, and does the same in `GetPointerMemorySpace` for consistency. Since there was no CUDA test for `IsHostMemoryPinned` so far, I also added some to `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_executor_test.cc`. (They pass with and without the initialization.)

When `WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion` sinks an `all-reduce` feeding a

head_commit.message:
Preserve 64-bit dynamic-slice split factors in AllReduceSplitter.

`AllReduceSplitter` previously narrowed the 64-bit quotient between the
`all-reduce` split dimension and the `dynamic-slice` slice size to a 32-bit
`int` before validating whether the slice represents a logical reduce-scatter.
When the 64-bit quotient was a multiple of 2^32, the narrowed factor became
zero and crashed compilation with `SIGFPE`; when it wrapped modulo 2^32 to a
negative or positive divisor of the replica group size, replica-group
construction crashed or evaluated a bogus split factor.

Keep split dimensions, slice factors, and group sizes as `int64_t` across
`AllReduceSplitter`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Re-record command buffers when symmetric memories change.

Even though currently thunks are not using symmetric memories directly in the kernels in theory it's possible through FFI (see relevant collective ops ffi test). Therefore once collective memory is re-created a corresponding graphs should be re-captured. Note that this change will detect only change of symmetrical memories associated to the collective memory space. If FFI thunk allocates its own symmetrical memories -- they won't be detected.

To detect this we give every `SymmetricMemory` a process-unique id that is never reused.
`CommandBufferThunk` remembers, per device, the (key, id) pairs of the symmetric
memories its command buffer was recorded with
(`CollectiveMemory::symmetric_memory_ids()`), compares them exactly and without
allocating against the current `CollectiveMemory` on every execution, and
replaces the command buffer with a new one when they differ.

Also add `CommandBufferRerecordsAfterCliqueDestroyed`, which replays a command buffer
with an FFI custom call that uses a symmetric memory, destroys the cliques, and
checks that the next execution re-records the command buffer.

head_commit.message:
PR #51992: [XLA:TSL] Check output buffer capacity in SnappyInputBuffer::Inflate

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51992

#ai-generated

**Status quo:** `SnappyInputBuffer::Inflate` checks the uncompressed block size against its output buffer with `DCHECK_GE` (`xla/tsl/lib/io/snappy/snappy_inputbuffer.cc:131`).

**Why:** The check disappears in release builds, so `Snappy_Uncompress` can write a block larger than `output_buffer_capacity_` into the output buffer.

**Design choices:** Return `absl::ResourceExhaustedError` before decompression when the block exceeds the configured capacity, with the same message format as `SnappyInputStream::Inflate` and the input buffer capacity check above it. A valid block can exceed a caller's configured capacity, so this is a sizing error rather than data loss. Add GoogleTest coverage for an exact fit, spare capacity, and rejection when capacity is insufficient. The successful cases also exercise multiple blocks and reset.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives:** Keep the existing fixed buffer capacity instead of allocating based on the input block. This change is confined to Snappy input buffering.

**Testing:** `bazel test //xla/tsl/lib/io/snappy:snappy_test` passes (12 of 12 tests) on Linux x86_64 with `-c opt` and with AddressSanitizer. Without the `snappy_inputbuffer.cc` change, `UncompressedBlockExceedsOutputBuffer` fails in the `-c opt` build because `Inflate` returns OK, and the AddressSanitizer build reports a heap-buffer-overflow write in the Snappy decoder called from `SnappyInputBuffer::Inflate`.

head_commit.message:
Preserve 64-bit dynamic-slice split factors in AllReduceSplitter.

`AllReduceSplitter` previously narrowed the 64-bit quotient between the
`all-reduce` split dimension and the `dynamic-slice` slice size to a 32-bit

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject out-of-range dimension indexes in ShapeInference

Four ShapeInference functions index a shape's dimensions with an
instruction- or caller-supplied value without checking it:

- InferReshapeShape uses inferred_dimension as the tie-break when a
  dynamic input dimension maps to several output dimensions, and
  passes it unchecked to set_dynamic_dimension.
- InferBatchNormGradShape bounds feature_index from above only, unlike
  the training and inference variants, and then reads
  dimensions(feature_index).
- InferTopKShape reads dimensions(-1) for a scalar operand.
- InferBitcastConvertShape formats dimensions(-1) into its error
  message for a scalar operand converted to a wider type.

The HLO parser and verifier call the last three on parsed modules.
Return InvalidArgument in each case. The reshape check sits at the
tie-break, so unused inferred_dimension values are still accepted.

Add regression tests and boundary-value controls.

display_title: Avoid recursion in EmitInstruction for indexing and elementwise ops

head_commit.message:
Avoid recursion in EmitInstruction for indexing and elementwise ops

`SubgraphConverter::EmitInstruction` only used an iterative worklist for elementwise ops. Indexing ops like `bitcast`, `transpose`, `reshape` and `slice` still recursed through `HloToMlir` and the operand provider, which costs a few KiB of stack per op. So a long enough chain of these ops inside a single fusion overflows the stack of the compiling thread. (We've seen fusions with chains of a few hundred bitcasts when `algsimp` is disabled.)

Therefore this change computes the operand indices when an instruction gets pushed onto the work stack and emits all in-subgraph operands iteratively before lowering the instruction itself. Ops with dedicated emitters (`pad`, `concatenate`, `dynamic-slice`, `reduce`, etc.) still request their operands through the operand provider, so chains of those still recurse. `HasDedicatedEmitter` is now the single list of these ops, and `HloToMlir` checks that it got indices for every operand otherwise.

The emission order changes from a reverse BFS to a DFS post-order. After canonicalization and CSE the IR is the same for all existing tests.

This also fixes two latent issues of the old elementwise worklist:

1. It emitted the broadcasted scalar operands of `select` and `clamp` with the full-rank output indices, which produced invalid IR like `tensor.extract %arg0[%x, %y] : tensor<i8>`. This went unnoticed because canonicalization removed the dead op before anything verified it.
2. Operands could get emitted twice because the reverse loop called `HloToMlir` without checking the cache first.

To catch issues like the first one, the test now verifies the IR before canonicalization.

head_commit.message:
Fix uninitialized reads in PrintAllocatorStatisticsNoLock

When an allocation fails, `GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::PrintAllocatorStatisticsNoLock` logs four memory pool attributes that it queries with `cuMemPoolGetAttribute`. If one of these queries fails, it logs the error but then still prints the value, which is uninitialized in that case.

So this change moves the query and the logging into a small lambda that initializes the value to 0 and only prints it if the query succeeded. The error message now also names the attribute.

Since none of the existing tests reached `PrintAllocatorStatisticsNoLock`, I also added a test to `xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_cudamallocasync_allocator_test.cc` that makes an allocation fail and checks that all four statistics get logged. (The query doesn't fail in the test, so it also passes without this change.)

head_commit.message:
PR #48378: [XLA:CPU] Do not send reductions with non-trivial reducers to YNNPACK

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48378

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`IsReduceLikeOpSupportedByYnn` only looked at the root of the reducer computation (`add`/`max`/`min` of the two parameters). If the reducer has any other instructions in it, for example a side-effecting outfeed like in the module from #47374, the reduce still got wrapped into a `__ynn_fusion`. The YNN emitter then hits `CHECK_EQ(reduce_instr->to_apply()->instruction_count(), 3)` in `DefineReduceOp` when the YNN executable is built on the first execution, so compile succeeds and the process aborts at run time. For `reduce-window` there is no CHECK and the extra instructions were just dropped.

This change makes the matcher require the reducer to be exactly the two parameters plus the root, which is the shape the emitter can actually express (same guard as in `all_reduce_key.cc`, `all_reduce_combiner.cc` etc.). Such reductions now take the regular CPU path instead.

Added two tests to `library_rewriter_test.cc` that run `LibraryRewriter` on a `reduce` and a `reduce-window` with an outfeed in the reducer and check that no YNN fusion is created. Both fail before this change.

Note that the module from the issue still does not compile on CPU after this change: it now hits the `computation_partitioner.cc:269` CHECK in the MLIR fusion emitter, which is the same crash site as #47373 and not YNN-specific.

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #47374. Process abort at run time on valid (if unusual) HLO with default flags.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/backends/cpu/transforms:ynn_matcher_test_cpu //xla/backends/cpu/transforms:library_rewriter_test //xla/backends/cpu/tests:ynn_fusion_test_cpu`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None (CPU only, covered by the unit tests above).

display_title: Add DumpHloSnapshotIfEnabled overload without HloModule

head_commit.message:
Add DumpHloSnapshotIfEnabled overload without HloModule

To decide whether to dump an HLO snapshot and to name the file, `DumpHloSnapshotIfEnabled` only needs the module's unique id, its name and its `DebugOptions`. The snapshot content itself comes from the executable's `HloProto`, so the `HloModule` isn't needed at all.

This change adds an overload that takes just these three values, so callers can dump snapshots without having an `HloModule` around. We will need that once executables materialize their module lazily (a follow-up switches `Service` and `Executable::dumping_snapshot` over to it).

The existing `HloModule` overload now delegates to the new one, so the behavior and the file names don't change.

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

head_commit.message:
Support GPU AOT results without an embedded HLO module

A `GpuExecutable` compiled without an embedded HLO module serializes to a `GpuExecutableProto` without `hlo_module_with_config.hlo_module`, but such a proto can't be turned into a `GpuAotCompilationResult` and loaded again. `GpuAotCompilationResult::FromProto` and `FromSerialized` always deserialize the module, which fails on the missing field. On top of that the split proto writer always creates an empty `hlo_module_with_config.hlo_module` (while normalizing backend configs and clearing the module id), so the reader can't tell anymore that there is no module.

Therefore this change makes the split writer, `GpuAotCompilationResult` and `GpuExecutable::FromProto` check for the inner `hlo_module` and only touch or deserialize the module if it's present. This also covers config-only protos, where `hlo_module_with_config` only has the `config` set. (`optimized_module()` is already nullable, and `GpuExecutable::FromProto` already handled a missing `hlo_module_with_config`.) Without a module, `GetCompiledMemoryStats` now computes the padded peak from the buffer assignment alone and reports the unpadded peak as 0 (unknown), and the `LoadExecutable` VLOG no longer dereferences a null module. Output and behaviour for executables with an embedded module are unchanged.

Note that this only fixes newly written artifacts. Module-less artifacts written by the old split writer contain an empty `hlo_module` and still fail to load, as they did before.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Share the additive scan combiner check between EmitScan and CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`, which requires the combiner root to be `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is a `kAdd`, optionally wrapped in a `kConvert`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts `convert(add)`. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs, where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output.

Make the default combiner in `ScanSupportTest` a valid `tuple(add, add)`, so that each existing negative test only fails on its own forbid condition.

Add a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48378

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`IsReduceLikeOpSupportedByYnn` only looked at the root of the reducer computation (`add`/`max`/`min` of the two parameters). If the reducer has any other instructions in it, for example a side-effecting outfeed like in the module from #47374, the reduce still got wrapped into a `__ynn_fusion`. The YNN emitter then hits `CHECK_EQ(reduce_instr->to_apply()->instruction_count(), 3)` in `DefineReduceOp` when the YNN executable is built on the first execution, so compile succeeds and the process aborts at run time. For `reduce-window` there is no CHECK and the extra instructions were just dropped.

This change makes the matcher require the reducer to be exactly the two parameters plus the root, which is the shape the emitter can actually express (same guard as in `all_reduce_key.cc`, `all_reduce_combiner.cc` etc.). Such reductions now take the regular CPU path instead.

Added two tests to `library_rewriter_test.cc` that run `LibraryRewriter` on a `reduce` and a `reduce-window` with an outfeed in the reducer and check that no YNN fusion is created. Both fail before this change.

Note that the module from the issue still does not compile on CPU after this change: it now hits the `computation_partitioner.cc:269` CHECK in the MLIR fusion emitter, which is the same crash site as #47373 and not YNN-specific.

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #47374. Process abort at run time on valid (if unusual) HLO with default flags.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/backends/cpu/transforms:ynn_matcher_test_cpu //xla/backends/cpu/transforms:library_rewriter_test //xla/backends/cpu/tests:ynn_fusion_test_cpu`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None (CPU only, covered by the unit tests above).

head_commit.message:
Add DumpHloSnapshotIfEnabled overload without HloModule

To decide whether to dump an HLO snapshot and to name the file, `DumpHloSnapshotIfEnabled` only needs the module's unique id, its name and its `DebugOptions`. The snapshot content itself comes from the executable's `HloProto`, so the `HloModule` isn't needed at all.

This change adds an overload that takes just these three values, so callers can dump snapshots without having an `HloModule` around. We will need that once executables materialize their module lazily (a follow-up switches `Service` and `Executable::dumping_snapshot` over to it).

The existing `HloModule` overload now delegates to the new one, so the behavior and the file names don't change.

display_title: Support GPU AOT results without an embedded HLO module

head_commit.message:
Support GPU AOT results without an embedded HLO module

A `GpuExecutable` compiled without an embedded HLO module serializes to a `GpuExecutableProto` without `hlo_module_with_config.hlo_module`, but such a proto can't be turned into a `GpuAotCompilationResult` and loaded again. `GpuAotCompilationResult::FromProto` and `FromSerialized` always deserialize the module, which fails on the missing field. On top of that the split proto writer always creates an empty `hlo_module_with_config.hlo_module` (while normalizing backend configs and clearing the module id), so the reader can't tell anymore that there is no module.

Therefore this change makes the split writer, `GpuAotCompilationResult` and `GpuExecutable::FromProto` check for the inner `hlo_module` and only touch or deserialize the module if it's present. This also covers config-only protos, where `hlo_module_with_config` only has the `config` set. (`optimized_module()` is already nullable, and `GpuExecutable::FromProto` already handled a missing `hlo_module_with_config`.) Without a module, `GetCompiledMemoryStats` now computes the padded peak from the buffer assignment alone and reports the unpadded peak as 0 (unknown), and the `LoadExecutable` VLOG no longer dereferences a null module. Output and behaviour for executables with an embedded module are unchanged.

Note that this only fixes newly written artifacts. Module-less artifacts written by the old split writer contain an empty `hlo_module` and still fail to load, as they did before.

display_title: Fix int32 overflow in GetAllGatherTransformations stride accumulation

head_commit.message:
Fix int32 overflow in GetAllGatherTransformations stride accumulation

`GetAllGatherTransformations` passed `int` literal `1` as the initial value to
`absl::c_accumulate` when computing `all_gather_num_strides`, truncating the
prefix dimension product to 32-bit `int` before widening to `int64_t`. When the
prefix stride product exceeds `INT32_MAX`, the narrowed accumulator either
misses valid within-shard reshapes or wraps modulo `2^32` to falsely match an
incompatible across-shard reshape and scramble data across replicas.

Initialize the accumulator with `int64_t{1}` and add unit tests covering both
modulo-`2^32` collision rejection and `>INT32_MAX` within-shard reordering.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

`EstimateNumWarps` picks the warp count from the largest padded tile in the fusion. Broadcasts, `iota` and narrow intermediates such as `pred` comparisons feeding a reduction inflate that size by 4x or more, which selects 4-8 warps where 2-4 are faster.

Count operand and root tiles in full and ignore non-root `broadcast` and `constant` tiles. Size non-root `iota` by its extent along `iota_dimension`, and scale non-root array tiles other than dots by `min(element_bytes, 4) / 4`.

This relands cl/1008957649 (rolled back in cl/1010131399) without its `blocks_per_core` change to the compute-time estimate, which regressed an inference benchmark by 1.5-1.66x. Dot tiles are now counted in full, since dots accumulate in 32-bit registers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012020591

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Drop unused LLVM target AsmParsers from IrCompiler

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Drop unused LLVM target AsmParsers from IrCompiler

`IrCompiler::EmitMachineCode` lowers LLVM IR directly to an in-memory object buffer via `TargetMachine::addPassesToEmitMC` (`Target`, `TargetInfo`, `TargetMC`, and `AsmPrinter`), and XLA:CPU never emits CPU inline assembly (`llvm::InlineAsm` or module-level inline asm), which is the only LLVM codegen path that invokes `Target::createMCAsmParser`. Remove the unused `LLVMInitialize*AsmParser()` registrations from `InitializeTargets()` (and `ir_compiler_test`) and replace `//xla/tools:llvm_targets` on `//xla/backends/cpu/codegen:ir_compiler` with the per-architecture `@llvm-project//llvm:*CodeGen` dependencies already used by `:jit_compiler`, avoiding linking ~2.5 MB of unused target MC assembly-parser tables and code.

Runtime and memory impact: None (neutral to slightly faster one-time initialization). Target `MCAsmParser` factories were previously registered in `TargetRegistry` during `InitializeTargets()` and never instantiated during compilation or execution; generated machine code and peak memory usage are unchanged.

Preserve 64-bit DynamicUpdateSlice offsets in while all-reduce motion.

When `WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion` sinks an `all-reduce` feeding a
`dynamic-update-slice` out of a `while` loop, `UpdateSliceContext`
tracks slice offsets as `int64_t` and materializes `S64` start-index

construction iterated with `int`, truncating offsets above `INT32_MAX`.

Widen the offset loop variable in
`xla/hlo/transforms/collectives/while_loop_all_reduce_code_motion.cc`
to `int64_t` so 64-bit slice offsets are preserved without narrowing.

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

head_commit.message:
PR #51932: [XLA:CPU] Gate broadcast division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51932

📝 Summary of Changes
Modified the check for the optimization to rewrite A / broadcast(B) to A * broadcast(1 / B)
only when fast math is enabled.
Keep the original division when fast math is disabled.
Add unit tests for both fast-math enabled and disabled case

🎯 Justification
A * (1 / B) introduces an intermediate rounded reciprocal, so it can produce a different floating-point result from A / B.

When fast math is disabled, the simplifier should preserve the original division semantics. This affects workloads using broadcasted divisors, such as per-row or per-sample scaling.

Resolves #51148.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
NA

🧪 Unit Tests:
Updated AlgebraicSimplifierTest to verify:
 - Without fast math, A / broadcast(B) remains a division.
 - With fast math, it is rewritten to A * broadcast(1 / B).
 - Updated ScalarDividePredicate to explicitly enable fast math
    since it relies on the same rewrite.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No Execution tests were added.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Drop unused LLVM target AsmParsers from IrCompiler

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Drop unused LLVM target AsmParsers from IrCompiler

`IrCompiler::EmitMachineCode` lowers LLVM IR directly to an in-memory object buffer via `TargetMachine::addPassesToEmitMC` (`Target`, `TargetInfo`, `TargetMC`, and `AsmPrinter`), and XLA:CPU never emits CPU inline assembly (`llvm::InlineAsm` or module-level inline asm), which is the only LLVM codegen path that invokes `Target::createMCAsmParser`. Remove the unused `LLVMInitialize*AsmParser()` registrations from `InitializeTargets()` (and `ir_compiler_test`) and replace `//xla/tools:llvm_targets` on `//xla/backends/cpu/codegen:ir_compiler` with the per-architecture `@llvm-project//llvm:*CodeGen` dependencies already used by `:jit_compiler`, avoiding linking ~2.5 MB of unused target MC assembly-parser tables and code.

Runtime and memory impact: None (neutral to slightly faster one-time initialization). Target `MCAsmParser` factories were previously registered in `TargetRegistry` during `InitializeTargets()` and never instantiated during compilation or execution; generated machine code and peak memory usage are unchanged.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use int64_t accumulator in GetBatchRowColumnShape

`GetBatchRowColumnShape` in `xla/service/gpu/matmul_utils.cc` passed literal
`1` (`int`) as the initial value to `absl::c_accumulate`, deducing a 32-bit
`int` accumulator and narrowing 64-bit GEMM batch, row, and column dimension
products back to `int`. Extents exceeding `INT32_MAX` either wrapped negative
and failed shape validation or wrapped positive (`>= 2^32`) and silently
truncated `MatrixLayout` dimensions and strides. Initialize the accumulator
with `int64_t{1}` to preserve 64-bit extents, and add unit tests covering
`> INT32_MAX` and `> UINT32_MAX` GEMM shapes.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO after RunBackend

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Upload optimized HLO after RunBackend

**Status quo**
`GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` calls `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols(module.get())` and `MaybeUploadGpuSymbolMapping` before `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` executes. `RunBackend` subsequently mutates the `HloModule` during `RunPreSchedulingPasses`, `ScheduleGpuModule` (which sets the `HloSchedule`), `RunPostSchedulingPipelines`, and `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, and then registers the scheduled `HloModule` with `XlaDebugInfoManager` inside `GpuExecutable::Create`.

**Why**
Because `RunBackend` mutates and schedules the `HloModule` after `RunHloPasses`, the `HloModuleProto` uploaded at the end of `RunHloPasses` lacks the `HloSchedule` and post-scheduling transformations present in the `HloModuleProto` registered with `XlaDebugInfoManager` for profiling, producing a different fingerprint ID.

**Design choices**
- Move `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` and `MaybeUploadGpuSymbolMapping` from `GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` to `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` right after `GpuExecutable::Create` succeeds.
- Record the `unoptimized_fingerprint` returned by `MaybeUploadUnoptimizedGpuSymbols` in `GpuCompiler::RunHloPasses` in a mutex-guarded map keyed by `module->unique_id()`, and extract it at the start of `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` to upload the unoptimized-to-optimized symbol mapping once `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` returns `optimized_fingerprint`.
- Add `GpuCompilerTest.UploadsOptimizedHloAfterRunBackend` to verify that `RunBackend` uploads the scheduled `HloModuleProto` and that its fingerprint ID matches the profiled `HloModuleProto` collected from `XlaDebugInfoManager::StopTracing`.

**Compromises**
- Callers that invoke `RunHloPasses` without `RunBackend` (such as `EarlyExitPoint::kAfterLayoutAssignment`) do not produce a scheduled backend executable and therefore do not upload an optimized `HloModuleProto`.

**Alternatives**
- Keep `MaybeUploadOptimizedGpuSymbols` in `RunHloPasses` and strip schedule and post-scheduling changes before fingerprinting in the profiler. Rejected because profiling consumers require the final scheduled `HloModuleProto` that actually executes on the GPU.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1011555676

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Require additive scan combiners in CanTritonHandleScan.

`EmitScan` only supports scans whose combiner outputs are `kAdd`, because it pads out-of-bounds elements with zero. `CanTritonHandleScan` accepted any associative combiner, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create Triton scan fusions (e.g. for a max scan) that then fail to emit.

Forbid scans whose combiner root is not a tuple of `kAdd`s. Like `EmitScan`, look through a `kConvert` around the `kAdd`, which `FloatNormalization` may insert for `bf16`.

display_title: [XLA] Fix integer power lowering for odd bases with large exponents

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix integer power lowering for odd bases with large exponents

Iterate exponentiation-by-squaring over the full integer bit width rather
than stopping after 6 iterations in both ElementalIrEmitter::EmitIntegerPow
and mapMhloOpToStdScalarOp<mhlo::PowOp>.

Stopping at 6 iterations ignored all exponent bits >= 6, producing wrong
wrapping modulo 2^N results for odd bases when exponent >= 64 (e.g. 3^64
evaluated to 3^0 == 1). Iterating over all bit_width bits consumes the
entire non-negative/unsigned exponent, which also makes the post-loop
even-base zeroing select redundant.

Fixes #50550.

head_commit.message:
Emit unique kernel symbols for deduplicated fusions under Nsight Compute or debug/line info

When profiling CUDA Graphs in Nsight Compute (`ncu --graph-profiling node`), build-time NVTX ranges are ignored and kernel targeting via `ncu --kernel-name` relies on the kernel symbol name. When `HloComputationDeduplicator` and `KernelReuseCache` merge identical fusions into a single deduplicated kernel symbol, `ncu` cannot isolate an individual HLO fusion instance.

Skip fusion deduplication in `HloComputationDeduplicator` and include the fusion name in `KernelReuseCache` lookup keys when `xla_gpu_generate_debug_info` or `xla_gpu_generate_line_info` is enabled, or when Nsight Compute environment variables are active.

head_commit.message:

When an allocation fails, `GpuCudaMallocAsyncAllocator::PrintAllocatorStatisticsNoLock` logs four memory pool attributes that it queries with `cuMemPoolGetAttribute`. If one of these queries fails, it logs the error but then still prints the value, which is uninitialized in that case.

Since none of the existing tests reached `PrintAllocatorStatisticsNoLock`, I also added a test to `xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_cudamallocasync_allocator_test.cc` that makes an allocation fail and checks that all four statistics get logged. head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Unwrap `kConvert` when checking for additive scans in Triton `EmitScan`.

On GPUs without `bf16` arithmetic (pre-Hopper CUDA GPUs such as A100), `FloatNormalization` rewrites the `bf16` `kAdd` of a scan combiner to `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))` with the add in `f32`, while the `kScan` stays `bf16`. `EmitScan` required every combiner root operand to be a `kAdd` and rejected these scans as non-additive.

Accept a `kAdd` wrapped in one `kConvert`. Zero is still the identity for the out-of-bounds padding, and the combiner body already emits the converts.

head_commit.message:
Preserve 64-bit dynamic-slice split factors in AllReduceSplitter.

`AllReduceSplitter` previously narrowed the 64-bit quotient between the
`all-reduce` split dimension and the `dynamic-slice` slice size to a 32-bit
`int` before validating whether the slice represents a logical reduce-scatter.
When the 64-bit quotient was a multiple of 2^32, the narrowed factor became
zero and crashed compilation with `SIGFPE`; when it wrapped modulo 2^32 to a
negative or positive divisor of the replica group size, replica-group
construction crashed or evaluated a bogus split factor.

Keep split dimensions, slice factors, and group sizes as `int64_t` across
`AllReduceSplitter`.

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

display_title: Fix stack buffer overflow in IsFabricMemory

head_commit.message:
Fix stack buffer overflow in IsFabricMemory

`IsFabricMemory` reads `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES` into a 4-byte `unsigned int`, but the driver writes a 64-bit value. So the call overwrites the 4 bytes after `handle_types` on the stack. In an x86-64 build with `-Os`, these are the low 4 bytes of the caller's saved `rbx` register.

This only leads to a crash if the caller keeps a live value in `rbx` across the call. After an unrelated change shifted register allocation, `CudaStream::Memcpy` now keeps its `ActivateContext` pointer in `rbx` and segfaults when it destroys that pointer.

So this change makes `handle_types` a `uint64_t`. The CUDA documentation doesn't state the type of this attribute, but NCCL and UCX both read it into a 64-bit integer.

I also added tests to `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver_test.cc` that only use driver API calls. For every pointer attribute and memory pool attribute that stream executor queries, they measure how many bytes the driver writes and compare that to the size of the variable that stream executor uses. They cover device, pinned host, pageable host, managed and VMM memory, and both `cuPointerGetAttribute` and `cuPointerGetAttributes`. Apart from `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES`, all of these variables already had the right size.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51881

📝 Summary of Changes

With >1 GPU per process, the per-GPU launcher threads raced to build + save an incarnation map in a shared per-process options structure. This could lead to heap corruption and deadlocks. This change saves the map made by each thread to a local copy of the options to avoid the race.

🎯 Justification

Fixes flaky deadlocks/crashes in JAX test `//tests/multiprocess:multihost_utils_test_gpu`.

head_commit.message:
Initialize results of pointer attribute queries in CudaExecutor

`cuPointerGetAttributes` returns `CUDA_SUCCESS` for pageable host memory but doesn't write `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_RANGE_START_ADDR` and `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_RANGE_SIZE`, even though the documentation says that the attributes get assigned default NULL values in that case. `CudaExecutor::IsHostMemoryPinned` only reads the range if the memory type is `CU_MEMORYTYPE_HOST`, so today it never reads the uninitialized values. But that's only due to the order of the checks.

So this change initializes the results in `IsHostMemoryPinned` to 0, and does the same in `GetPointerMemorySpace` for consistency. Since there was no CUDA test for `IsHostMemoryPinned` so far, I also added some to `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_executor_test.cc`. (They pass with and without the initialization.)

display_title: Fix stack buffer overflow in IsFabricMemory

head_commit.message:
Fix stack buffer overflow in IsFabricMemory

`IsFabricMemory` reads `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES` into a 4-byte `unsigned int`, but the driver writes a 64-bit value. So the call overwrites the 4 bytes after `handle_types` on the stack. In an x86-64 build with `-Os`, these are the low 4 bytes of the caller's saved `rbx` register.

This only leads to a crash if the caller keeps a live value in `rbx` across the call. After an unrelated change shifted register allocation, `CudaStream::Memcpy` now keeps its `ActivateContext` pointer in `rbx` and segfaults when it destroys that pointer.

So this change makes `handle_types` a `uint64_t`. The CUDA documentation doesn't state the type of this attribute, but NCCL and UCX both read it into a 64-bit integer.

I also added tests to `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver_test.cc` that only use driver API calls. For every pointer attribute and memory pool attribute that stream executor queries, they measure how many bytes the driver writes and compare that to the size of the variable that stream executor uses. They cover device, pinned host, pageable host, managed and VMM memory, and both `cuPointerGetAttribute` and `cuPointerGetAttributes`. Apart from `CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ALLOWED_HANDLE_TYPES`, all of these variables already had the right size.

display_title: Fix C++20, libc++, and CUDA 13.4.1 compatibility issues in XLA.

head_commit.message:
Fix C++20, libc++, and CUDA 13.4.1 compatibility issues in XLA.

Preparing XLA for upcoming C++20, LLVM `libc++`, and CUDA 13.4.1 toolchain upgrades surfaces three build and test issues:

1. In C++20 mode, `ABSL_CONST_INIT` expands to `constinit`, which requires `constinit` on both `extern` declarations and initializing definitions. Because `xla_op_utils.h` declares the `kHloSparseCoreV0*` string constants with `TF_CONST_INIT extern const`, defining them as `constexpr` in `oss/xla_op_utils.cc` triggers `-Wmissing-constinit`. Update the OSS definitions to `TF_CONST_INIT const` to match `google/xla_op_utils.cc`.
2. Unlike `libstdc++`, `libc++` annotates `std::mutex` with Clang thread-safety attributes (`capability("mutex")`). In `EngineHeuristicsBuilder_v8::build()`, `cudnn-frontend` conditionally locks and unlocks `get_heur_b_mutex()` across two separate `if (m_heuristics.mode == CUDNN_HEUR_MODE_B)` blocks around `detail::finalize(...)`, triggering `-Wthread-safety-analysis`. Replace the split `.lock()` and `.unlock()` calls with a scoped `std::lock_guard<std::mutex>`.
3. In CUDA 13.4.1, `nvJitLinkComplete()` can return `NVJITLINK_SUCCESS` even when `nvJitLinkGetErrorLog()` contains `ptxas` register spill diagnostics. Always fetch `nvJitLinkGetErrorLog()` and validate it with `CreateErrorFromPTXASLog()` before checking `linking_result`.

name: CI
display_title: Reuse scratch buffers in DelinearizeUsingTranspose to eliminate TCMalloc LockAndAlloc contention.

head_commit.message:
Reuse scratch buffers in DelinearizeUsingTranspose to eliminate TCMalloc LockAndAlloc contention.

In `DelinearizeUsingTranspose`, unpacking sub-32-bit TPU tensor layouts (`kPackingFactor > 1`, e.g., BF16/F16/S8/S4) previously allocated and freed a temporary `Buffer` (`> 256 KiB` for typical model outputs) on every tensor via `DefaultAllocator` (`malloc`/`free`). Under high-concurrency multi-output TPU model serving, these repeated `> 256 KiB` allocations miss TCMalloc's per-CPU caches, contend on `tcmalloc::tcmalloc_internal::HugePageAwareAllocator::LockAndAlloc` and `InvokeHooksAndFreePages`, and incur cold-page / page-fault overhead during the transpose.

Introduce `ScratchBufferPool`, an `absl::Mutex`-guarded pool of reusable power-of-two scratch buffers (`<= 32 MiB`, up to 16 entries sorted by capacity) released via `NoncopyableBuffer`'s custom deleter, falling back to `DefaultAllocator` when a buffer exceeds the cap or sanitizers are active.

head_commit.message:
When `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleReduceWindow` folds a `kPad` into a `kReduceWindow`, `is_effective_broadcast` replaces the pair with a broadcast of the unpadded operand. The check previously inspected only the `kPad` configuration and ignored existing padding and window dilation on the `kReduceWindow` itself. When the `kReduceWindow` also carried window padding, output windows that covered only padding elements were rewritten to the operand value. Window padding on dimensions larger than 1 also triggered a crash in `CreateBroadcastSequence`.

Compute the combined `Window` first and check `is_effective_broadcast` against that combined window and static shapes. Require trivial windows on dimensions not equal to 1, reject window dilation or negative padding on size 1 dimensions, and check endpoint window coverage. Existing programs whose combined window covers a single unpadded element surrounded by identity padding still fold to broadcast.
